title: Telemetry-driven shortpatch optimizer for idempotent admin utilities
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: Our support engineers execute frequent short fixes (shortpatches) during incidents. Current shortpatches are brittle: they can be non-idempotent, lack telemetry for success/failure, and are hard to rehearse in the sandbox. This ticket builds an optimizer for shortpatch packages that enforces idempotency patterns, wires rich telemetry, and suggests runtime fallbacks.

Goal: Produce a lightweight pipeline that validates and packages admin shortpatches into idempotent 'repairlets', automatically instruments them with telemetry and audit metadata, and exposes runtime suggestions (e.g., pre-checks, safe rollbacks, dry-run hooks) in the admin console and runbook runner. The optimizer should integrate with existing runbooks-as-tasks runtime and the ephemeral admin sandbox.

Success metrics: reduction in incident rollback rate for applied shortpatches by 40% in Q2, increase in shortpatch rehearsal coverage in sandbox to 90%, and telemetry adoption of repairlets above 80% for high-frequency incident actions.
acceptance_criteria: Optimizer can analyze a shortpatch snippet and report idempotency issues with actionable fixes
Generated repairlet packages include a dry-run mode that can execute safely in the ephemeral sandbox
Automatic telemetry is attached to repairlets: start/finish timestamps, outcome, actor, pre/post hash, and drift metrics
Repairlet execution is gateable by RBAC and emits structured audit logs compatible with KMS/HSM-backed keying decisions
Integration test that replays 50 historical shortpatches in the sandbox: no unsafe side-effects in dry-run, and at least 85% successful instrumentation
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha: Initial RFC and spike notes attached. Chose 'repairlet' naming for compactness and to avoid confusion with existing runlet/runpack terms.

2026-03-11 Luca: Completed static analyzer prototype for idempotency heuristics. Heuristics detect stateful file writes, unchecked DB migrations, and non-atomic network calls. Found ~22% of shortpatch corpus has at least one anti-pattern.
2026-03-12 PM review (Mina Patel): Request to add pre-check templates (quota checks, schema safety) to reduce runtime surprises. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-13 Security (Rajiv Shah): Security review requested. Will require audit fields and KMS integration for repairlet packages that touch secrets. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-14 Devops (Sofia): Sandbox replay harness updated to accept repairlet dry-run metadata. Wrote preliminary fixtures for 50 historical shortpatches.

2026-03-15 Luca: Implemented telemetry schema (repairlet_id, version, actor_id, outcome, pre_hash, post_hash, duration_ms). Open question: should we also emit per-step tokenized traces? Spike scheduled Cycle 12.
2026-03-15 Aisha: Flagged dependency on ENG-981999 (admin-conductor-priority-lane) for prioritized scheduled execution slots. Marked as dependency below.
risks: Non-idempotent fixes may still slip through heuristics; need manual review in high-risk namespaces
Telemetry volume: naive instrumentation could generate high cardinality metrics that spike observability costs
Integration with KMS for audit signing may add latency to repairlet deployment pipeline
mitigations: Require a manual approval step for repairlets that modify persistent state until heuristics recall improves above 95%
Sample telemetry at 10% by default and provide opt-in for full traces; add retention and cost alerts in Console
Implement asynchronous signing and optimistic rollout; fallback to unsigned artifact if KMS latency exceeds threshold with audit event recorded
implementation_notes: Analyzer component will be a standalone CLI + library (pkg: repairlet/analyzer) that can be invoked in CI and the admin console
Packaging format: Signed tarball with metadata.json containing idempotency-fix suggestions, dry_run entrypoint, telemetry schema, and RBAC scope
Runtime hooks: pre_check, dry_run, apply, verify, rollback. Each hook emits structured audit events to existing telemetry ingestion endpoint
Telemetry schema will mirror existing runbook tracing but add 'pre_hash' and 'post_hash' for drift detection
Add a 'repairlet-lint' GH action to block merging of unsafe shortpatch quickfixes into the internal snippets repo
qa_plan: Unit tests for analyzer heuristics with a curated corpus of safe/unsafe snippets
End-to-end replay in ephemeral sandbox using 50 historical shortpatches (provided by Support Ops)
Chaos test: simulate partial failures in pre_check and verify that rollback semantics are exercised
Telemetry validation: ensure events conform to schema and reconcile with backend by sampling 1000 runs
rollout_plan: Week 0: Deploy analyzer and packaging pipeline to staging. Run 50 historical dry-runs and collect results.
Week 1: Opt-in beta: expose repairlet packaging in Console to 10 internal teams. Collect feedback and iterate heuristics.
Week 2: Auto-instrument repairlets for low-risk namespaces. Require manual approval for high-risk namespaces.
Week 3+: Full rollout with monitoring dashboards and cost alerts; run formal postmortem after first 30 production repairlet runs
